subject: Dedicated capacity: burst/autoscale pricing and cooldown structure
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Eve Larson <eve.larson@fintech.co>; procurement@fintech.co
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity: burst/autoscale pricing and cooldown structure

Hi Eve —

Thanks for the runbook you sent during the demo. To follow up, attached is our current dedicated-capacity pricing doc (dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf). I pulled out the burst/add-on section into the first appendix, but wanted to call out a couple of questions so we can align on a recommended structure: 

1) Surge billing unit: would you prefer per-GPU-hour surcharged at peak (linear) or purchased surge credits (slab packs that auto-decrement)?
2) Cooldown semantics: are 15/30/60 minute cooldown windows acceptable, or do you need per-request cooldown exemptions for scheduled ETL jobs?
3) Throughput guarantees: do you require a per-minute TPS guarantee for inference or a per-token 99th percentile latency SLO?
4) Reserved commit sizing: do you want to commit by GPU count or by sustained throughput (tokens/sec)?

If you can share a 14-day tail of peak-minute usage (one CSV is fine) that would let us model the right slab sizes.

Suggested next step: 30-min call this week to walk pricing variants and an example 12-month commit with burst lanes. Are you available Wed or Thu morning PT?

Attachments: dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing + burst appendix)

Best,
Grace
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.example
(415) 555-0192
From: Eve Larson <eve.larson@fintech.co>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 11:04:17 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: burst/autoscale pricing and cooldown structure

Grace —

Thanks for the doc. Quick answers and context:
- We run a mixed workload: latency-sensitive user-facing chat (bursty mornings) and large-batch ETL model scoring overnight. Peak-minute concurrent GPUs historically hit 28 GPUs, sustained nightly average ~8 GPUs.
- Our procurement team prefers predictable monthly cost. They will push for a committed GPU count with an overage/burst mechanism.
- Cooldowns: for scheduled jobs we need a bypass; otherwise 30-minute cooldown is fine.
- Throughput SLA: we'd ask for a 95th-token-latency SLA for user-facing endpoints and a best-effort throughput for batch.

I've attached our procurement_form_fintech.pdf (standard PO language + billing window). We're targeting a go-live in Q4, prefer a 12-month term if we can get predictable economics.

Can your team propose: (A) a 12-month commit with baseline GPUs + burst credits and (B) a month-to-month option with higher overage rates?

Eve Larson
Head of Platform Operations, Fintech Co.
eve.larson@fintech.co
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 14:30:05 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: burst/autoscale pricing and cooldown structure

Folks —

Looping you in on Fintech Co.'s reply. Key asks: 12-month commit preferred, baseline commit by GPU count, need bypass for scheduled batch, 95th-token latency SLO for user-facing. They want two proposals: committed + burst credits, and month-to-month with higher surge rates.

Questions for pricing:
- How aggressive can we get on slab credits vs linear surcharges while keeping margin?
- Suggested cooldown default = 30m with opt-out for scheduled jobs (technical enforcement ok?).
- Any recommended language for throughput SLA and financial credits (percent-of-monthly-bill)?

Ben/Marissa — can you draft a short comparison and a suggested anchor price for the committed option? I want to send a clean proposal back to Eve by EOD Tues.

Best,
Grace
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:00:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: burst/autoscale pricing and cooldown structure

Grace —

High-level proposal (numbers are illustrative; I can produce an exact model):

Option A — 12-month commit (preferred):
- Baseline: 16 reserved GPUs (monthly commit).
- Burst: 3 slab sizes: 
  * Small pack: 40 GPU-hours (covers ~2–3 short peaks) at $X per GPU-hour (effective ~20% discount to on-demand surge)
  * Medium pack: 160 GPU-hours at better unit price
  * Large pack: 480 GPU-hours at best unit price
- Cooldown: default 30-minute cooldown that prevents immediate re-bursts. Scheduled jobs can present a signed schedule file that exempts them from cooldown enforcement.
- Throughput SLA: 95th-token-latency SLO with service credit = 3% of monthly bill per missed SLO window, capped at 15% monthly credit.
- Discount: 18% off published on-demand dedicated hourly rate for a 12-month commit (with step-down to 15% if they commit to 24 months).

Option B — Month-to-month:
- No baseline commit; on-demand dedicated rate + surge at 1.6x on-demand for ad-hoc bursts.
- Slab packs available as prepayment add-on (smaller packs only).

Notes:
- Slab packs reduce invoicing volatility (easier for procurement) and make unit economics more predictable for them. Offer a buy-back clause for unused credits at 25% if they churn early.
- Cooldown enforcement needs product involvement but is doable; exemption by signed schedule is a reasonable process.

If we want to be aggressive to close, we could make the Large pack effectively give them ~25% discount versus on-demand for sustained bursts.

Ben
Director, Sales Engineering
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:22:37 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity: burst/autoscale pricing and cooldown structure

Ben / Grace —

A few tweaks from pricing/ops perspective before we send to Fintech Co.:

1) Slab sizing: given their peak of ~28 GPUs, propose baseline 20 GPUs (16 under-delivers) and a Large pack sized to cover 24 GPU-hours/day for the first month of on-peak usage. That gives them breathing room and keeps uplift predictable.
2) Cooldown: 30 minutes default is fine. For scheduled ETL bypass, require a 72-hour advance schedule file submitted to billing ops to avoid abuse.
3) SLA: make the credit logic simpler: 1% of monthly committed spend per SLA miss up to 10% cap. Keep language narrow to user-facing endpoints only; exclude batch jobs.
4) Legal/Procurement: move the buy-back clause into a credit note vs cash refund.

I'll attach a short SOW draft and the pricing_table_slabs.csv for their review. If we want to offer a one-time onboarding credit (waived first month of surge fees) that could act as a sweetener without impacting committed pricing.

Marissa
Principal Product Pricing
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Eve Larson <eve.larson@fintech.co>, procurement@fintech.co
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: burst/autoscale pricing and cooldown structure

Eve —

Thanks again for the details. Based on your usage profile we've put together two clean options (attached): 

1) 12-month Commit (recommended) — baseline 20 reserved GPUs, slab-based burst credits (Small / Medium / Large), 30-minute cooldown default with a scheduled-job exemption process (72-hour advance notice), 18% committed discount, SLA limited to user-facing endpoints with credit cap at 10% of committed monthly spend, and a 1-month onboarding waiver for surge fees.

2) Month-to-month — on-demand dedicated + 1.6x surge rate for ad-hoc bursts; small slab packs available as prepay add-ons.

Attachments: SOW-draft.docx, pricing_table_slabs.csv (breakdown by pack), dedicated_pricing_v2.pdf (for reference).

Next steps: could we schedule a 30-min call Thurs 10:00 AM PT to walk the SOW and finalize procurement language? If procurement prefers, we can also provide a redline-ready DocuSign for the 12-month commit.

Open items we plan to include in the formal proposal: final baseline GPU count (you suggested peak 28; we proposed 20 baseline + slabs), exact unit prices for each slab, buy-back mechanics as credit note, and explicit SLA exclusion for batch jobs.

If that sounds good I can loop legal and ops and send a formal proposal after the call.

Best,
Grace
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
